title: .complete should take elements into account
body: The [specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#dom-img-complete) for `.complete` disregards image sources from a `` element. > If any of the following are true: > - both the src attribute and the srcset attribute are omitted; > - the srcset attribute is omitted and the src attribute's value is the empty string; > - the img element's current request's state is completely available and its pending request is null; or > - the img element's current request's state is broken and its pending request is null, Given the following example. (Assume that the `lazy load resumption steps` and `Fetch the image` haven't been invoked yet.) ```html ``` Per spec, `.complete` should be true as the first bullet applies. Both the `src` and the `srcset` attribute on the image are omitted. This seems a bit off. The `selected source` is set to the the url from the `` element, and the image `lazy load resumption steps` is set to fetch the image from the selected source at a later point. In the [source](https://github.com/whatwg/html/blob/main/source) there's a comment from 2016 that seems to indicate that it was intended to check sources in the `` parent: > \ Should the spec be updated to account for the selected source? When the `src` and `srcset` attributes is omitted by authors, returning `true` would still be unexpected if there's a `current request` for a selected source who's state is not `completely available` or `broken`. Additionally, only Firefox follows the spec and returns true for the case above, while Chrome and Safari returns false.
